st: Rinse the rice in cold water until clear, then soak for 20 minutes and drain.
Heat [[3 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onions for 10 minutes until deep golden.
Stir in the garlic, cinnamon stick, cardamom, and [[2 tbsp]] baharat for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and brown on all sides for 6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[2 tbsp]] tomato paste, dried limes and [[2 tsp]] salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in [[4.5 cups]] water, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Lift out the chicken. Add the drained rice to the pot, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on very low heat for 18 minutes.
Meanwhile, brown the chicken under a hot broiler for 5 minutes.
Rest the rice covered for 5 minutes, fluff, and serve topped with the chicken.

ing: such as hammour, snapper or cod, in pieces
st: Rinse [[2 cups]] rice until the water runs clear and soak it for 20 minutes.
Rub the fish with [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric and [[1 tsp]] salt and let sit for 10 minutes.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot and fry the fish for 2 minutes per side until lightly golden. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot add [[2 tbsp]] oil and cook the onions for 10 minutes until golden.
Stir in the garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] coriander and [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, dried limes, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[3.5 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and simmer 10 minutes.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot. Cook uncovered on medium until water is almost absorbed, about 8 minutes.
Lay the fish on top, cover tightly, and cook on low heat for 12 minutes until the rice is tender and the fish flakes.
Let stand 5 minutes, then serve the fish on the rice.
Soak [[2 cups]] wheat in plenty of cold water overnight, then drain.
Put the lamb, wheat, cinnamon stick and [[10 cups]] water in a heavy pot. Bring to a boil and skim the foam.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2.5 hours, stirring now and then, until both are very soft.
Remove the lamb, take out the bones, and shred the meat finely.
Return the meat to the pot and remove the cinnamon stick.
Beat the porridge with a heavy wooden spoon or potato masher for 10 minutes until smooth and sticky like a thick porridge.
Season with [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and simmer 10 more minutes, adding hot water if too thick.
Serve in a wide bowl with a well in the center and pour in [[3 tbsp]] melted butter.
Dust with [[1 tsp]] ground cinnamon and, if you like, [[1 tbsp]] sugar.
Soak [[2 cups]] cracked wheat in water for 1 hour, then drain.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a large pot and cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, [[2 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] coriander, [[0.5 tsp]] turmeric and cinnamon stick and stir 1 minute.
Add the chicken and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Pour in [[8 cups]] water with [[2 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper. Simmer, covered, for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Remove the chicken, shred the meat, and discard bones.
Add the wheat to the broth. Cook on low, covered, for 45 minutes, stirring often.
Return the chicken and mash the mixture with a spoon until thick and creamy.
Serve hot with [[2 tbsp]] melted butter poured over the top.
Soak a pinch of saffron in [[2 tbsp]] hot water for 10 minutes.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pot over medium heat and fry the vermicelli for 3 minutes until golden brown.
Add [[2 cups]] water, [[0.33 cup]] sugar, [[1 tsp]] cardamom and the saffron with its water. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the noodles are tender.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] rose water and [[1 tbsp]] butter and keep covered and warm.
Beat the eggs with [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet and cook the eggs without stirring for 3 minutes until fully set, as a thin omelet.
Mound the vermicelli on a plate and lay the omelet on top. Serve warm.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan.
Steep a pinch of saffron in [[2 tbsp]] warm milk for 10 minutes.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] baking powder, [[1 tsp]] cardamom and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Beat [[0.5 cup]] butter with [[0.75 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the saffron milk and [[1 tbsp]] rose water.
Fold in the dry ingredients, then stir in [[0.25 cup]] milk, only until smooth.
Pour into the pan and bake 35 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out and serve warm or at room temperature.
Soak a pinch of saffron in [[2 tbsp]] warm water for 10 minutes.
Whisk [[1.5 cups]] flour, [[2 tbsp]] cornstarch, [[1 tsp]] yeast, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom and [[0.25 tsp]] salt.
Pour in about [[1 cup]] warm water and the saffron and whisk to a thick, sticky, pourable batter.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until bubbly and doubled.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Oil a spoon, scoop up small bites of batter and slide into the oil. Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and puffed.
Drain the fried balls on paper towels.
Drizzle with [[0.5 cup]] date syrup and serve at once while crisp.
